_note: Hand-labelled category ground truth for the Phase 2 evaluation harness (docs/10 §5.1, docs/04 §11).
The KEY is a fragment `description` exactly as `@finmate/nlp` extracts it from the v1 golden
dataset in packages/nlp/test/golden/fixtures/, so the two datasets cannot drift: the parser
expectations stay where they are and this file adds only what a category should be.
A description belongs in exactly one of the two maps. `paths` means a human can name the category
from the text alone; `shouldAsk` means no category can be defended from the text alone, so the
correct behaviour is to ask (calibrated confidence < 0.60) rather than to guess.
`dataset.spec.ts` fails if a description in the golden fixtures appears in neither map, so this
table cannot silently fall behind the dataset.

`voda` is deliberately a PATH, not a should-ask: `merchants.ts` makes `voda` an alias of the `Vodovod` merchant, so the shipped knowledge does name a category for it, and the first harness run showed the ambiguity note was the label's error rather than the pipeline's (docs/04 §8.1.5).

shouldAsk.Idea storno: A storno (cancellation) of an Idea purchase — the direction is clear, the category is the original purchase's.
shouldAsk.Kafa: Capitalised variant of `kafa` — same ambiguity, same deliberate 1.0 weight.
shouldAsk.Lidl vraćeno: A refund at Lidl: the category of the refund is the counterpart of the original purchase, which the text does not state.
shouldAsk.Maxi vraćeno: A refund at Maxi, same as `Lidl vraćeno`.
shouldAsk.Stan: Rent/strawberry? — "stan" here is an apartment (rent), and the tree has no rent category.
shouldAsk.kafa: Ambiguous by design (docs/04 §8.1.3): buying coffee is `Kafa i kolači`, but "kafa i mleko" is groceries. The tree weights `kafa` at 1.0 (corroborating) for this reason.
shouldAsk.kirija: Rent has no category in the shipped tree; the user must choose rather than have one invented.
shouldAsk.kupovina: The word means "purchase" and names no category at all — 66 of the 300 v1 cases are exactly this, and the correct behaviour is to ask, not to guess.
shouldAsk.popravka: Ambiguous between `Automobil / Servis` (weight 2) and `Kuća / Održavanje` (weight 1): the text alone cannot say whether the car or the house was repaired.
shouldAsk.refund Lidl: A refund at Lidl, same as `Lidl vraćeno`.
shouldAsk.storno Lidl: A storno of a Lidl purchase, same as `Idea storno`.
shouldAsk.vraćeno: A direction (money came back), not a category. The tree has `Povraćaj` for a *refund*, but "vraćeno" alone does not say what was returned or by whom.
shouldAsk.vraćeno Maxi: A refund at Maxi: the category is the original purchase's, which the text does not state.
